Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one complete NEW whole painted skyline panel for a 360-degree game background, NOT a collage or a crop. Genuine RGBA transparency. The attached game scene is ONLY a matte game-rendering-style reference: do not copy its palace, foreground or person. The attached sky is ONLY a warm-light/palette reference: do not include sky, clouds, sun, paper, matte, checkerboard or any opaque background in this panel.
Show the ordinary city surrounding the Forbidden City in Beijing circa 1900, seen looking outward from the palace near Taihemen. The palace itself is outside the picture, behind the viewer. A dense fine-grained carpet of low GREY tiled hutong and siheyuan courtyard houses, grey brick lanes/walls, scattered dark green cedar/acacia tree crowns. Roofs are distinctly cool dark grey, warm sunlight may touch their edges. No second Forbidden City, no duplicated imperial complex, no yellow/orange palace roofs, no giant red palace halls. Yellow glazed roofs are allowed ONLY on the five specified Jingshan hill pavilions in the NORTH panel. No modern architecture, skyscrapers, cars, electricity pylons, people, animals, text, logos, compass symbols or labels. No fantasy mountain panorama or Great Wall.
One approximately 2000x1106 landscape canvas, aspect 100:55.3. Equirectangular angular band: exactly100 degrees left-to-right and elevation+35.6 at the top to-19.7 at bottom; geometric horizon at y64.38%. Central90 degrees plus5 degrees on each end for10-degree neighbor overlap. Keep the far-left and far-right10% quiet, low and misty: only tiny grey rooftops/trees, no distinct tall landmark cut by an edge. Consistent common low architectural baseline around y65%, naturally irregular roofline. Most ordinary architecture occupies y49%-68%, northern hill may rise to y37%. Large transparent headroom. Lower roof/tree details must dissolve softly into thin pale atmospheric haze and then true alpha0 by y85%; absolutely no straight hard ground edge, slab, opaque fog rectangle or drop shadow. Empty alpha0 space above skyline and below its feathered haze.
Restrained, detailed matte painterly game art; readable roof eaves and varied individual courtyard blocks, smooth natural surfaces, no repeated stamped/AI pattern, no canvas-grain overlay, no black outline. Nearby colors clear; distant city becomes pale blue-grey through aerial haze. Late-afternoon sunlight from compass258 degrees (west-southwest), elevation19 degrees, same light across all four panels. Warm golden side highlights, cool soft shadows; do not paint a sun disk. Do not add more landmarks than this direction calls for. Whole scene is distant background artwork, no foreground gameplay buildings.

DIRECTION SPECIFICATION:
NORTH panel: center azimuth0 (North), coverage310 through0 to50 degrees clockwise. The nearby Jingshan wooded hill is centered exactly x50%, broad enough to see EXACTLY FIVE small separate pavilions on its ridge: one modestly taller central pavilion and two small pavilions on each side. Only these five hill pavilions may have subdued yellow glazed roofs. Below the hill: only GREY ordinary courtyard roofs, no yellow-roof palace or grand imperial gate. At x20% (azimuth330, northwest), a modest distant Beihai WHITE DAGОBA: one white Tibetan stupa body and dark pointed finial on a wooded rise, not a multi-storey pagoda. At x70% (azimuth20) a tiny far Deshengmen city gate tower with DARK GREY roof, partially softened by haze. Keep all three features at different sensible scales; Jingshan is the nearest focal landform. No Temple of Heaven here.
